Over its checkpoints 1 to 11 the stem policy never passes 10/100 (averaged weights: 0, 1, 0, 3, 5, 5, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6).

Where it fails (checkpoint 9, averaged weights; 30 layouts rolled out with every control step recorded): in 16 it never closes within 3 cm of the named stem; in 13 the stem is held by the test above at some step, but the hold lasts 3-9 steps before a finger loses the stem; 1 succeeds.

Over the closed steps within 3 cm of the named stem, no finger touches it 56% of the time, the stem is outside the fingertips' depth 32% of the time, outside the jaws sideways 20%, the gripper outside the band 20%.
The first close is nearest the named stem in 60% of episodes (chance 33%): the flowers' heads are themselves look-alikes (red, orange, pink).

The evaluation now also reports `caught_rate`, the share of episodes in which the named object was held (stems) or lifted at any step: for the final stem policy, 52/100 caught and 6/100 held for 10 steps.
Executing 4 actions per chunk instead of 8 does not help (1/100, caught 40/100).
Where it goes wrong shows when the expert drives the first K control steps toward the named stem and the policy takes over (final checkpoint, averaged weights):
| Expert drives | Grasp the stem (10 steps) | Caught at some step | First close nearest the named stem | Cut the named stem (3 steps) |
| nothing | 6/100 | 52/100 | 60% | 9/100 (19 other stems cut) |

rows.detail: 1 s; the expert's close comes at about step 60
quotes: | 20 steps (1 s; the expert's close comes at about step 60) | 7/100 | 83/100 | 88% | |
One second of the expert is enough to make the policy catch the named stem most of the time, so the first failure is at the very start: committing to a stem and a side.

The expert takes the side whose path in passes farthest from the other stems, so in a given layout either side is about as likely, and the two sides need opposite turns of the wrist from the first step.
A second failure is holding still: even started well it keeps the stem for 10 steps in only a tenth of the episodes, though for 3 steps (a cut) in about 60%.

`collect.py --expert_side preferred` makes the side follow from where the stem stands: in from the outer edge of the table toward its middle, the other side only when that path passes within 4 cm of another stem.
The expert cuts 90/100 that way (92/100 with the clearance rule).
A first version, always the side away from the front camera, cut only 73/100: it failed on stems right of the robot's middle line (20 of 36).

Each flower is built as a base and a top part (upper stem and head) held by a weld; when the test of step 4 holds on a stem for 3 control steps in a row, the stem is cut at the gripper's height (clipped to the band) and the top part falls.
Cutting the named stem is a success; cutting any other ends the episode as a failure.
